Two New Android Auto Features Google Is Secretly Working On
11 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution/Google
Judging from the number of bugs found by Android Auto users, Google would be quite busy in the next couple of months if the focus were entirely on stability and reliability. However, the search giant is also working on several new features, and two of them have just been uncovered.
We’ve known for a while that Google was planning a major Android Auto update called Cielo, so these new discoveries aren’t necessarily surprising. Google is planning a major transformation of Android Auto, and it looks like almost every corner of the app will receive more or less substantial improvements.
Dual-SIM status bar icons If you’ve been part of the Android Auto space for more than a few weeks, you probably know that one of the biggest struggles here was the cellular icon signal indicator.
This one disappeared long ago due to a bug that even Google apparently struggled to deal with. After a long wait, it’s now coming back, and it looks like Google is also preparing an upgrade.
Photo: Google with autoevolution edits The company will show dual-SIM status bar icons for devices with two SIMs, finally addressing a limitation that has always been haunting Android Auto. Right now, if the phone you’re using to run Android Auto has two SIMs, it still shows just one cellular icon, assuming you even see this one, given the bug mentioned earlier.
This new “feature” was spotted in Android Auto 18.0, but it’s not live yet for production devices. Google is probably holding it back for a later launch, possibly as it wants to align its introduction with the debut of the Cielo update.
The new phone calling experience One of the biggest benefits of having Android Auto running on your infotainment screen is that you can continue to focus on the road while you still interact with your phone - with Gemini when you’re in motion or with touch when you’re parked.
It’s no secret that the phone calling experience hasn’t always been the most refined, either due to problems with Google Assistant or Gemini or because of limitations in Android Auto itself.
For example, if a contact in your phonebook has more than one phone number, Android Auto is asking what number you want to use every time you try to call that contact. This happens both with touch and with Gemini, as Android Auto needs to make sure it’s dialing the right number.
Photo: AndroidAuthority That could soon change, as Android Auto will let users choose a default number for contacts with multiple numbers and remember the number you used the last time. It’ll be interesting to see how the whole thing is going to work once it goes live, but for users, this is a big improvement, considering they’ll spend less time messing with Android Auto for such a simple thing like a phone call.
The new phone calling experience also includes a new interface for the dial pad. When you open the Phone app on Android Auto, you’ll still see the old interface that debuted three years ago when the Coolwalk visual refresh came out.
That’ll change soon as Google is bringing Material 3 Expressive to this part of the Android Auto interface, too, as spotted in Android Auto 18.1.. The redesigned UI uses larger buttons with backgrounds, improving readability and making it easier for drivers to use the dial pad.
The big “2026” update In addition to these two announced changes, Google is also working on finalizing the update that it announced in the spring of 2026.
The Cielo update will be the most significant redesign of the Android Auto interface since the introduction of Coolwalk in 2023 and will include plenty of new features, such as widgets and support for video apps. Google has also been caught working on an animated character to show the weather forecast on the screen, presumably as it might end up giving up on the dedicated weather card appearing only on portrait units.
The support for video apps will allow Android Auto users to watch videos while their cars are stationary, with an audio-only mode to kick in when motion is detected. This means you’ll be allowed to continue the playback when you start driving, only that video will be restricted, whereas the audio will continue in the background.
Photo: Google YouTube will pioneer this new feature in the Android Auto space, and users will need a YouTube Premium subscription for the audio-only option.
Google will also update Android Auto to use the entire screen estate on displays with unusual shapes and dimensions, such as the ones in MINI cars, where the carmaker installed circular screens. In its current form, Android Auto only appears on the center of the screen using a rectangular panel, while the Cielo update will expand the app to the entire screen, therefore getting a circular appearance.
This major refresh was originally expected in 2026, but it’s now more likely to land in the first months of 2027. The first users could still get it in December, but broad availability will certainly be reached next year.

2027 Kia EV6 Pricing Remains the Same As Last Year For All Seven Trims, But So Do All the Features
7 photos
Photo: Kia
Kia America has revealed that it doesn't care about inflation for this year's Kia EV6, but unfortunately the model built in West Point, Georgia, is also a carryover from MY2026.
The US division of the South Korean automaker reported at the beginning of October 2026 its best-ever month of September with 77k units and a very good third-quarter sales tally of almost 237k vehicles, growing by 18% and eight percentage points, respectively. Hybrids did great, and so did no less than eight popular models: Seltos (+66 percent); Niro (+47 percent); K4 (+43 percent); Telluride (+42 percent); Sorento (+37 percent); Carnival (+21 percent); K5 (+15 percent); and Sportage (+10 percent).
Year-to-date, the company is at 667,386 units, up from 636,148 las year and well on their way toward establishing a new full-year sales record. As such, the brand is continuing strong with the announcements for the 2027 model year pricing and details for various models like the Sorento, Sorento HEV and PHEV, EV3, and now also the EV6. The latter is completely carried over from last year, and the MSRP of all seven trims remains the same, along with the destination fee of $1,545.
“In doing so, Kia America remains committed to providing value to consumers. With the EV6 MSRP pricing unchanged and the launch of the all-new EV3 all-electric SUV, Kia is making EVs more attainable for those who embrace the fully electric lifestyle,” explains the company. So, the 2027 Kia EV6 Light SR RWD starts at $37,900 sans destination, followed by the Light LR RWD and AWD at $41,200 or $45,200.
The Wind RWD and AWD grades are $44,800 or $48,800, while the GT-Line RWD and AWD cost $48,700 and $53k, respectively. The base model has 167 horsepower and a 63-kWh battery pack, which is enough for up to 237 miles of range. The two Light Long Range (RWD and AWD) have 225 or 320 hp, respectively, and share the 84-kWh battery pack with the Wind and GT-Line models, as well as the hp ratings. They also share the range ratings: 319 miles for RWD and 295 miles for AWD.
All 2027 Kia EV6 models have some shared features: 19-inch alloy wheels, full LED headlamps and taillamps, glossy exterior mirror covers, the black “digital” tiger face design, the 12.3-inch color TFT LCD panoramic curved display cluster, a cargo power outlet, heated front seats, a leather steering wheel, dual-zone AC, a 12.3-inch Navi unit with Android Auto, Apple CarPlay, HD radio, SiriusXM, and an integrated modem, USB-C charge ports front and back, power windows, and Smart Key, among others.
So, what do you think? Did Kia do enough for the EV6 by keeping the pricing unchanged from last year or should they have also introduced some new features on top of that?

2026 Paris Motor Show • 1971 Nissan Skyline 2000GT-R Is Now an 833-Piece Mattel Brick Shop Set That Can Be Customized
This Audi RS6 Avant Has Bugatti Veyron-Rivaling Power
6 photos
Photo: Instagram | mtmautomotive
Audi has an entirely new A6 in its lineup. The C9-generation model entered production a little over one and a half years ago, yet the true range-topping member of the family is still in the making.
That would be the Audi RS 6, in case you forgot, which will continue to take on the likes of the BMW M5. And just like its big rival in the class, it will be offered in two body styles. That’s right, the RS 6 Sedan is making a comeback after well over a decade. The last time the company made such a thing was for the C6-generation RS 6, as the C7 and the C8 that followed were offered strictly as five-door station wagons.
Audi’s upcoming RS 6 was supposed to be christened the RS 7. That’s because the brand wanted to market its ICE models with odd numbers, reserving the even numbers for the EV family. However, it turned out to be confusing for its clientele, so the automaker decided to drop this scheme. But not before launching the new A5, which is the successor to the old B9 A4. And rumor has it that it might be rechristened the A4 again for the mid-cycle refresh.
Now, Audi Sport may not have a BMW M5 competitor in its lineup today, but the old RS 6 remains a great driver’s car. In fact, this model continues to make headlines today for different reasons, and it is often the tuned examples that catch our attention. Case in point, meet the latest that has made us want to share it with you, namely the black unit pictured in the gallery, which came directly from MTM’s portfolio.
Photo: Instagram | mtmautomotive And while it may stand out from the crowd very easily due to the extras on the outside, the icing on the cake lies under the hood. The quoted tuner hasn’t said exactly what it has done to the powertrain in order to make it this punchy. However, it has more oomph than some of today’s supercars. The magic number is 1,001 horsepower, and the output is likely metric. This would translate to 987 brake horsepower and 736 kilowatts.
We’d very much want to tell you about the thrust, 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) acceleration time, and revised top speed of this particular Audi RS 6, but the truth is that we do not know these aspects, as the tuner hasn’t released them at the time of writing. Nevertheless, it is probably safe to assume that we are looking at a vehicle capable of sprinting to the 62 mph mark in less than three seconds.
How do we know that? Because the Audi RS 6 can do it in a little over 3 seconds with no outside intervention, pushing up to 155 mph (250 kph), which is its electronically limited top speed. The 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine churns out 630 metric horsepower. That’s 621 horsepower for brake crowd and 463 kilowatts. As for the maximum thrust, it is officially rated at 627 pound-feet (850 Nm).
This modded Audi RS 6 Avant is street legal, MTM says, and besides packing a jaw-dropping amount of power to the point where it is up there with the original Bugatti Veyron, which is considered to be the world’s first hypercar, it also sports some special things on the outside. These include the new apron with blades on the sides, a tweaked grille, and a new hood, from what we can tell.
Photo: Instagram | mtmautomotive It seems that the trim on the front fenders is also on the very special side of things , just like the side skirt attachments. The decals on the front doors reveal its output in metric horsepower, the rear diffuser is new, and so are the roof-mounted wing, and the spoiler mounted below the rear windscreen. Some special badges further tell bystanders that they are looking at a very special machine, and the wheels round off the makeover.
The new alloys have a very intricate design and a black overall look, and they spin around the red brake calipers with white branding on them. The car features multiple other black touches on the outside, and the color is dark gray. We cannot see the interior in these pictures that MTM released on its social media channels recently, but in a perfect world, it would be mostly black, perhaps with a few touches of red here and there for a bit of contrast.
Do you want to make your Audi RS 6 Avant look like this, with the carbon fiber details and the new wheels mentioned above, and do you also want it to break into the four-digit output territory? In that case, you will have to reach out to MTM to discuss the details, because the finances have not been mentioned. But do you dig this spec? What about the immense amount of power available via the right pedal? View this post on Instagram A post shared by MTM Automotive AG (@mtmautomotive)
